item.title: Minnesota's Jonathan Kuminga looking like player Warriors hoped he'd be
item.description: Minnesota Timberwolves forward Jonathan Kuminga, the seventh overall draft pick by the Warriors in 2021, helped the Warriors win the championship in his rookie season. (Charlie Neibergall/Associated Press) MINNEAPOLIS - Anthony Edwards has seen, all along, what the Golden State Warriors have seen but couldn't make fit. When Jonathan Kuminga attacks the man in front of him, he is rarely stoppable. When he is handed the reins, and given command of a basketball, he is power and strength and a kind of off-the-hardwood athleticism that is in the 1%, at this level. It was everything else, really, that strained Kuminga's relationship with Golden State until it broke, inconsistent playing time and inconsistent vision and public contract-extension fussings leading to the unceremonious ship to Atlanta for Kristaps Porzingis in February. The Kuminga era, the idea of Joe Lacob's two-timeline approach, is over and gone in the Bay Area. Kuminga, though, still has plenty of fans on Golden State's staff. Believers, even. And he has landed in a situation in Minnesota, alongside the exuberant Edwards and under head coach Chris Finch, where the former No. 7 pick may truly and finally find himself. "Yeah, y'all see what's going on," Edwards said in a viral video in September , welcoming Kuminga upon his arrival in Minnesota. "This s- over with. Run this s- up." On Wednesday, in Minnesota, the Warriors will come face to face with a version of their former heir that - through four games - has been streamlined. After reportedly taking less money in free agency to land on a two-year, $13 million deal with the Timberwolves, the 23-year-old Kuminga has looked the part of a ready and willing secondary offensive valve (47% from three-point range) and lockdown point-of-attack defender (a 37.5% field goal percentage surrendered as the primary defender, per the NBA ). The baseline stats haven't popped off the page: 11.5 points, 5.8 rebounds, 2.5 assists in 29.8 minutes a game. But Kuminga has run the floor. He has scrapped. He has endeared himself to Finch, a known players coach whom Steve Kerr has offered heady praise for. "He's doing everything we asked him to do," Finch told reporters in Minnesota on Sunday, "or that he said he wanted to do when he came here about guarding, and defending, and hustle plays, that kind of stuff … and then he's just really letting the ball come to him, and he's trusting the offense and his teammates, and he's getting a lot of good looks 'cause the ball's really moving, and he's just playing within flow." item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images John Harbaugh did not scream when he saw his Giants lose to the Saints. He told the team the performance was “disgusting.” This word choice from the new coach reveals a strict standard that goes beyond simple anger. The Giants lost 34-27 in East Rutherford, but the real story happened two days later in a team meeting. Jon Runyan Jr. shared the details with the New York Post , noting that the theme of the day was clear. Harbaugh’s reaction shows he will not accept letting the team down, even after a couple losses. The Word Was Disgust, Not Anger Most fans expect a coach to yell when a team plays poorly. Harbaugh took a different path during that “pretty uncomfortable” meeting. Runyan Jr. told the Post, “I don’t know if it was anger,” but clarified the coach’s actual feelings. He said, “his word would probably be disgust. I think that’s the correct word — disgust.” This distinction matters because anger is often a fleeting emotion, while disgust implies a deep rejection of the effort shown. The Giants had let themselves down, and they had let Harbaugh down. The meeting was not about blaming one player but addressing a collective failure. The context for this meeting was the 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints. In that match, the squad Harbaugh constructed regressed significantly. For everyone present, his expression was incredibly transparent to the players. Runyan Jr. noted that the theme of that day was disgust. The coach’s reaction signals that he expects a specific level of intensity every single week. If the team cannot meet that bar, they will face his full disapproval. This sets a tone for the rest of the 2026 season. A Coach Who Reads Faces Harbaugh’s ability to read his own emotions helps him communicate with players. He did not hide his feelings from the Giants roster. According to reports, his facial expressions were remarkably transparent throughout the meeting. This transparency forces players to look at their own performance without excuses. It was a key moment for the team to reset before their next game. The Giants had let themselves down in East Rutherford. They failed to execute the plan that Harbaugh put in place. The coach’s use of the word “disgusting” shows he views this loss as a personal betrayal of the team’s identity. Runyan Jr. confirmed the intensity of the moment. The players knew exactly where they stood with their new head coach. There was no sugar-coating the 34-27 defeat. This reaction tells us exactly what to expect from Harbaugh in 2026. item.title: 3 quick takeaways from Badgers exhibition win over Oklahoma State: There are a couple things to work on
item.description: Wisconsin guard Owen Foxwell (15) heads downcourt on a fast break during the first half of their preseason game against UW-Green Bay Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026 at the Resch Center in Green Bay, Wisconsin. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Wisconsin Badgers beat the Oklahoma State Cowboys 82-65 on Tuesday evening in their final exhibition game ahead of the regular season, which begins on Monday evening. In the win, Wisconsin had its fair share of ups and downs and faced some late danger, but still came out with a comfortable win after a strong start thanks to strong three-point shooting and quality defense. For the second straight game, it was Owen Foxwell leading the way for Wisconsin, as he had 19 points, hitting all three of his three-pointers, while dishing out another three assists. Four other Badgers hit double figures, as Wisconsin went with the same starting group for the third straight game, with Victory Onuetu and Jack Janicki joining Foxwell, Eian Elmer, and Nolan Winter in the starting lineup. Here are three takeaways from Wisconsin’s exhibition win over Oklahoma State on Tuesday. Highs and lows of the offense Tuesday showed the strengths and current issues of Wisconsin’s offense, which had stretches of strong efficiency and rough lulls. Wisconsin started off the game on a 12-3 run over the first five minutes, which extended to 20-7 by the second media timeout. However, after a strong start to the half, the Badgers tapered off in the final minutes, as they didn’t score from the 5:57 mark to the 1:27 mark, much of which was with Owen Foxwell on the bench. Foxwell has been the clear key to this offense the last two games, both as a scorer and importantly, as a facilitator who initiates the ball movement. Wisconsin still saw a lot of ball movement, assisting on 17 of their 24 field goals, but they had a few stretches where they struggled to score without Foxwell on the court. In the second half, Wisconsin had two other stretches of nearly 2.5 minutes and nearly 3 minutes without points, allowing Oklahoma State to chip away at the lead. Overall, we saw Wisconsin push up-tempo very well and move the ball well for threes. That led to them shooting 18 of 41 (43.9 percent) from deep, while assisting on 17 of their 24 field goals. Wisconsin also got to the free throw line 22 times. But we also saw how Wisconsin’s offense doesn’t always have that go-to guy currently, especially if Foxwell isn’t on the court, leading to some cold spells. The Badgers also had a few too many stretches of sloppy basketball, recording 15 turnovers, although Oklahoma State was even worse with 22 turnovers. Wisconsin’s scheme and coaching will help configure another efficient offense, and this group has shown promise. There are just a few things to iron out. item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 12: Zay Jones #17 of the Arizona Cardinals catches the ball against Rodney Thomas #25 of the Indianapolis Colts in the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals had a very deep receiver room when the regular season began. And now, they traded away Marv Harrison and then Jalen Brooks became injured and subsequently had surgery, which placed him on IR. The once-very deep receiver room became a bit too shallow for the Cardinals coaching staff, so GM Monti Ossenfort brought in four receivers for workouts, plus a quarterback. RELATED: CARDINALS PLACE JALEN BROOKS ON IR The five players included QB Jack Plummer, and receivers Zay Jones, James Proche, Xavier Guillory, and Ronnie Bell. After the workout, Arizona inked Jones to a contract. Jones played for the Cardinals during the 2024 and 2025 seasons. In his final year, he tore his Achilles in Week 10 against the Seattle Seahawks and was placed on season-ending IR. Arizona did not re-sign him, and during free agency he inked a one-year deal with the Houston Texans. He had a good training camp, but was released on the final cutdown. He played in 19 games with the Cardinals, with two starts. Jones had 29 targets, 20 receptions for 267 yards, converted 12 first downs, a 13.4-yard-per-catch average, 55 YAC, and one drop. That drop was against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 3 last year, when the Cardinals had the game won if Jones caught the ball. Instead, they punted, and San Fran won the game in the last seconds on a field goal. A win would have given Arizona a 3-0-0 record. item.title: Toto Wolff reveals how Williams' surprise victory helped him secure Mercedes role
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes chief Toto Wolff revealed a jibe at Pastor Maldonado that helped him get his place on the team, as the Austrian businessman gave a comparison between the star Mercedes drivers and the then-Williams driver. Wolff was a shareholder and executive at Williams in 2012, when Maldonado took a surprising victory in the Spanish Grand Prix. At the time, Mercedes had won just once since returning as a works team in 2010, with Nico Rosberg ’s victory in China earlier that season. Speaking on the Cheeky Pint podcast with Stripe co-founder John Collison, Wolff said that the win with Williams was followed by a call from the Mercedes parent company. “One of the board members approached me and invited me to Stuttgart, and he said, ‘How can it be that your private little team can win a race, and we, Mercedes, we can’t do any better than that?’” Wolff said. After being given access to the team’s figures, Wolff asked the board what it expected from its F1 programme. The answer was world championships, and the Austrian told them their ambitions did not match the team’s spending. Toto Wolff, Mercedes Toto Wolff, Mercedes “I said, ‘OK, then one of us is wrong because I’m working on the same budgets, and I’m thinking about finishing in the top six.’ They said, ‘No, it’s not the same budget. Look, we spend 100 million more.’ “I said, ‘Yeah, those 100 millions you spend on Michael Schumacher and Nico Rosberg, I have a pay driver from Venezuela,’ who won the race, by the way, Pastor. ‘That’s the main difference.’ They didn’t like that situation at all. I said, ‘I’m just a messenger, and I’m going to go back to Williams.’” Maldonado, who brought substantial backing from Venezuela to Williams, beat Fernando Alonso to win in Barcelona from pole. It remained the only grand prix victory of his F1 career. Mercedes later returned with an offer. “Eventually, they came back and said, ‘We think our model, a corporate running a Formula 1 team, doesn’t function, because it needs to be much more entrepreneurially led, you need to be empowered to make decisions on the spot, and we want you to run this.’” Wolff said he initially turned the role down because he was a shareholder in Williams, but Mercedes offered to help him buy into the team instead. He joined Mercedes at the start of 2013, and the team went on to win eight consecutive constructors’ championships from 2014 to 2021. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

However, as jobs began opening across the country, it appears that the former Notre Dame and LSU head coach is getting the itch to return to the sideline as soon as 2027. Former LSU and Notre Dame Football Coach Brian Kelly Expresses Interest in Maryland Opening Last week, Maryland was the first school to fire their head coach, Mike Locksley. On Saturday, North Carolina State fired Dave Doeren, and Baylor fired Dave Aranda after a loss to Kansas over the weekend. There are likely going to be more jobs open by the end of the season. However, Kelly appears to be lobbying for the Maryland job when he joined College Sports Radio on SiriusXM. “They’re all unique, right? You know, we’re talking about ACC, Big 12, and and and the Big Ten,” said Kelly.“From a conference standpoint, the Big Ten obviously has proved itself to have that kind of appeal, right? With Maryland, it is a fertile recruiting area. There’s no doubt that that DMV area is a really good recruiting area. I think they’ve done great things in terms of upgrading facilities.” Yes, the DMV is a great area to recruit in, but it’s not a slam dunk that you’re going to be able to retain players. item.title: Potential Early Pirates Trade Candidates This Offseason
item.description: The Pittsburgh Pirates are always a team ready to make a trade, and their offseason should be no exception to that. Here are three early trade candidates currently on Pittsburgh’s roster. Paul Skenes Trade rumors surrounding Paul Skenes started well before the superstar pitcher made his MLB debut in 2024. There’s no reason to think that they’re going to stop this winter. In fact, trade speculation has already begun, with a recent report suggesting his salary could be outside Pittsburgh's comfort zone as early as next season. Pittsburgh shouldn’t be actively searching to move Skenes this winter. However, if the front office deep down knows that they have no chance of keeping the All-Star long-term, they at least have to entertain the idea of what If the Pirates get a trade package they simply can’t refuse, it wouldn’t be shocking to see Skenes moved before Opening Day 2027. Jul 27, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Pirates starting pitcher Mitch Keller (23) delivers a pitch against the Arizona Diamondbacks during the first inning at PNC Park. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Mitch Keller It might be time for the Pirates to move on from Mitch Keller. He’s had some high moments in Pittsburgh, but even the best partnerships might come to an end. With that in mind, Keller being traded this winter wouldn’t be the most shocking move of all time. Keller’s stats haven’t been great over the last few years and aren’t headed in the best direction, either. He finished the 2026 season on the injured list after recording a 5.29 ERA in 22 starts. However, Keller is still under team control as a starter for the next eight seasons, and that’s more valuable than some realize. There’s likely at least one team out there that would take a flier on him. Plus, if Pittsburgh feels they need to trade Keller to recoup any sort of value on his contract extension, this offseason would be the time to do it. Ryan O’Hearn Would the Pirates really trade Ryan O’Hearn just one year after signing the veteran to a two-year free agent contract last offseason? It’s certainly possible. O’Hearn’s first season in Pittsburgh was solid; it wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t great either. His .770 OPS in 2026 declined from where it was in 2026, but it was still above the 33-year-old’s career average. In a world where the Pirates potentially lose out on re-signing Brandon Lowe , the front office could once again commit to a young core for the 2027 season. In that case, exploring trade scenarios surrounding O’Hearn could make a lot of sense. The upcoming free agent class isn’t as strong as in past years. A team searching for a veteran hitter might need to turn to trade rather than signing, and that’s where a potential O’Hearn trade could arise.

item.title: Paul Finebaum opens up about receiving death threats: ‘That did concern me’
item.description: Credit: Awful Announcing Paul Finebaum knows a thing or two about riling up sports fans. He also knows what it feels like when things go too far. The ESPN and SEC Network host has made a career out of saying things that fire up SEC fans , and given the passion that rules that kind of college football fandom, it has sometimes come back on him in scary ways. During his appearance on The Awful Announcing Podcast last week , Finebaum discussed times when reactions to his hot takes went from heated to potentially life-threatening. Speaking with host Brandon Contes, Finebaum revealed that early in his career, as a columnist and reporter for the Birmingham Post-Herald and later as a radio host, some of his criticism of the Crimson Tide’s struggles turned into very personal, potentially scary backlash. “It’s gotten to a point where if you are not 100% cheerleader, you may not keep your job very long,” Finebaum said. “So I think that creates the stigma that… if you write something even mildly objective or report something, you are going to be ostracized because… it’s a little bit like politics. And it wasn’t always that way. It was that way when I started. It got away from it, and now it’s right back to where it started again. “… The death threats came in the mid to late ’80s. I was covering Alabama post-Bear Bryant. And I was born in the South, but my mother, father, and sister are all from New York City. So I had this different type of upbringing. “College football wasn’t particularly important to me. My dad was a Yankees fan. I followed the New York teams. I followed the New York media. And I’ll never forget, I was in New York in the ’80s. covering an Alabama game, and it was on a Friday night, and the Yankees had won like 110 games… And Warner Wolf was the local sports guy, and he said, ‘What?’ He said, ‘This is laughable. They won 110 games, and they got nothing. They stink.’ And I’m like going, you know, that really resonated with me. And I was a big fan of Howard Cosell growing up. So that’s what I did. “When I got to Alabama, I didn’t know you were supposed to do anything different. And it caused a lot of problems. And there have been a couple of threats. There was a threat about 2008 or ’09, just as the internet was really blowing up. Somebody put my home address with a MapQuest [map] online and said, ‘You will die on Saturday night.’ Now that did concern me a little bit. “We turned it over to authorities, and for about 2 weeks the radio station I worked for had a security guy follow me, and it got to be so ridiculous. item.title: Chatham tops Madison in Morris County Tournament field hockey final
item.description: BOONTON — When Ava Ewing was a freshman, she was scared to be on the field during the Morris County Tournament field hockey final. But she also couldn't forget the happiness when Chatham won the title . Now a senior co-captain, Ewing made sure the Cougars understood both sensations as they faced Madison for the MCT plaque again on Oct. 27. And Chatham came through to give Ewing that winning feeling again, 2-1 against the Dodgers. It is the Cougars' sixth MCT championship, but the first since a three-peat streak that stretched until 2023 – when the current seniors were freshmen. They have won nine games in a row dating back to Oct. 5, with the NJSIAA Tournament up ahead . Like the MCT champion Chatham girls soccer team a few days earlier, the field hockey bus was met by a police escort on the way back through town. "It's so awesome. I'm so happy," said Ewing, a defensive midfielder who plans to play at Brown University. "I told them how great of a feeling this is. It's so different being a leader. I was the one looking up to everyone freshman year. I was trying to play based on the people around me. But now, I'm bringing my teammates confidence." More: Morris County Tournament 2026 field hockey bracket, schedule, scores Senior forward Molly Chazen scored both Chatham goals and was named the offensive MVP of the final. The first came from the right side midway through the third quarter. But Madison senior Celia Stuart equalized less than five minutes later on a clean hit from about 10 yards out. The winning goal was opportunistic, as Chazen poked home a rebound. Her older sister, Emmy Chazen, had scored the winning goal with no time left on the clock when Chatham beat Madison in 2023. The younger Chazen described this title as "a full circle moment for us, and she's a big role model for me." Madison had been the two-time defending champions , and came into the MCT final on a four-match winning streak. These two teams have won all but one of the past nine titles. More: NJSIAA releases pairings for 2026 field hockey tournament Most of the players also know each other through their club teams: Centercourt and New Heights. Despite the Dodgers' tears, there were also many hugs and words of consolation exchanged after the final. "It definitely makes it more intense, because we know how everyone plays," said Chazen, who has verbally committed to Colgate. "Knowing the other players makes it more high stakes." item.description: Jamarion Batemon interviews during the Big 12 Media Days event at T-Mobile Center. | William Purnell-Imagn Images After serving as an electric shooter from the bench, Jamarion Batemon will look to increase his role on a Cyclone roster that lost some significant pieces from beyond the arc in the off-season. Batemon is one of many recruits to come from Wisconsin during the Otzelberger tenure, hailing from Milwaukee. Batemon was largely hot and cold throughout the season, bouncing between unstoppable from beyond the arc to some games being dreadful. If Batemon wants to maintain his starting spot in front of some other dynamic shooting guards, especially once Killyan Toure returns from injury. What does Batemon bring? The immediate impact he has is from beyond the arc. Over two-thirds of his total field goal attempts came from beyond the arc, where he would shoot at a 37% clip. As is the life of a sharp shooter, Batemon had his highs and lows. Against Alcorn State, he went off for a season high 26 points while going 7-10 from deep. While everyone remembers the Heise three pointer against Houston, Batemon hit a huge three right before it to take a one point lead with 2:10 remaining in the game. In the NCAA tournament, Batemon went just 3-15 from deep, which is certainly below what the Otzelberger staff is looking for. Defensively, Batemon recorded 21 steals, which is impressive once you account for the amount of minutes he averaged and having two of the best on ball defenders in the country taking some of those steal opportunities. How will Batemon be used? Of the returning roster, Batemon has the highest three point average. It doesn’t take a rocket scientist to expect Batemon to be used in a similar fashion as last year, but with more playing time with the departure of Milan Momcilovic. In the two exhibition games, Batemon has shot 4-15 from deep and amassed 22 points. My personal take is that he is simply shaking off some of the rust of the off-season, and those totals should improve with games being played with more regularity. Defensively, Batemon will not be asked to defend whomever the leading scorer on the opposing team is, as that title will likely be taken on rotation of Jaquan Johnson, Tamin Lipsey and eventually Killyan Toure. That doesn’t mean that Batemon won’t have a significant presence on defense, as he will often be asked to shut down the next available option as the first option either gets put in the toureture chamber, gets set in front of Lipsey, or just gets bullied by Jaquan Johnson. Another year in the Otzelberger defense, another year in the weight room, and hopefully another year of developing into the next Cyclone sharpshooter.

item.description: The Minnesota Timberwolves , after a 3-1 start to the season that showed that the backcourt connection of guards Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball was going to be as thrilling and productive as believed, have just received some devastating news about their franchise's biggest star. Per a report from ESPN's Shams Charania , Edwards will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee that could keep him sidelined for up to two months. Edwards' right knee has been bothering him since last season, with inflammation in the right knee being a recurring reason that contributed to keeping Edwards sidelined for 21 games last season and leading him to miss the 65-game requirement for end of season awards.
